original_abstract: Omnidirectional scene text detection has received increasing research attention. Previous methods directly predict words or text lines of quadrilateral shapes. However, most methods neglect the significance of consistent labeling, which is important to maintain a stable training process, especially when a large amount of data are included. For the first time, we solve the problem in this paper by proposing a novel method termed Sequential-free Box Discretization (SBD). The proposed SBD first discretizes the quadrilateral box into several key edges, which contains all potential horizontal and vertical positions. In order to decode accurate vertex positions, a simple yet effective matching procedure is proposed to reconstruct the quadrilateral bounding boxes. It departs from the learning ambiguity which has a significant influence during the learning process. Exhaustive ablation studies have been conducted to quantitatively validate the effectiveness of our proposed method. More importantly, built upon SBD, we provide a detailed analysis of the impact of a collection of refinements, in the hope to inspire others to build state-of-the-art networks. Combining both SBD and these useful refinements, we achieve state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks, including ICDAR 2015, and MLT. Our method also wins the first place in text detection task of the recent ICDAR2019 Robust Reading Challenge on Reading Chinese Text on Signboard, further demonstrating its powerful generalization ability. Code is available at this https URL.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting multi-oriented and irregularly shaped scene text in natural images, which remains a difficult problem due to variations in text orientation, scale, and aspect ratio. Building on recent advances in single-shot detectors and direct regression methods, the paper proposes a novel end-to-end framework that combines corner localization with adaptive region refinement to achieve both high accuracy and efficiency. Unlike previous methods that rely on complex post-processing or indirect regression, the proposed approach directly predicts text boundaries through a unified network, reducing computational overhead. The method is evaluated on multiple benchmarks, including ICDAR2015, TotalText, and COCO-Text, where it achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of F-measure and inference speed. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively handles arbitrary-shaped text while maintaining real-time processing capabilities, making it suitable for practical applications such as autonomous navigation and mobile OCR systems. The paper contributes a new method for scene text detection that advances the field by addressing limitations of existing approaches.

original_abstract: Conventional cross-domain image-to-image translation or unsupervised domain adaptation methods assume that the source domain and target domain are closely related. This neglects a practical scenario where the domain discrepancy between the source and target is excessively large. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to learn domain adaptive features between the largely-gapped source and target domains with unlabeled domain bridges. Firstly, we introduce the framework of Cycle-consistency Flow Generative Adversarial Networks (CFGAN) that utilizes domain bridges to perform image-to-image translation between two distantly distributed domains. Secondly, we propose the Prototypical Adversarial Domain Adaptation (PADA) model which utilizes unlabeled bridge domains to align feature distribution between source and target with a large discrepancy. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed models.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) when multiple source domains are available, a scenario that is more practical but less explored than the traditional single-source setting. Building on prior work that aligns feature distributions using adversarial training, moment matching, and classifier discrepancy, this paper proposes a novel method that integrates these approaches to better handle multi-source domain adaptation. The proposed approach dynamically aligns feature distributions across multiple sources and a target domain by leveraging both domain-invariant features and task-specific decision boundaries. It introduces a new objective function that combines moment matching with classifier discrepancy to ensure that the target features are not only domain-invariant but also lie within the support of the source data, avoiding ambiguous regions near class boundaries. The method is evaluated on a large-scale multi-source UDA dataset, demonstrating superior performance over existing methods in both image classification and segmentation tasks. The paper concludes that combining distribution alignment with task-specific constraints leads to more robust and effective domain adaptation, particularly in multi-source scenarios. This work is an empirical study that advances the state of the art in multi-source UDA.

original_abstract: The revolution in computer hardware, especially in graphics processing units and tensor processing units, has enabled significant advances in computer graphics and artificial intelligence algorithms. In addition to their many beneficial applications in daily life and business, computer-generated/manipulated images and videos can be used for malicious purposes that violate security systems, privacy, and social trust. The deepfake phenomenon and its variations enable a normal user to use his or her personal computer to easily create fake videos of anybody from a short real online video. Several countermeasures have been introduced to deal with attacks using such videos. However, most of them are targeted at certain domains and are ineffective when applied to other domains or new attacks. In this paper, we introduce a capsule network that can detect various kinds of attacks, from presentation attacks using printed images and replayed videos to attacks using fake videos created using deep learning. It uses many fewer parameters than traditional convolutional neural networks with similar performance. Moreover, we explain, for the first time ever in the literature, the theory behind the application of capsule networks to the forensics problem through detailed analysis and visualization.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the growing challenge of detecting face manipulation in videos, particularly as synthetic media becomes increasingly realistic and pervasive. Building on recent advances in deep learning and the availability of large-scale datasets such as FaceForensics++, the paper proposes a novel multi-stream neural network architecture that integrates both global and local features to improve detection accuracy. Unlike prior methods that focus on still images or single-stream models, this approach leverages temporal information through recurrent convolutional strategies and incorporates domain-specific preprocessing techniques. The proposed method is evaluated on benchmark datasets, including FaceForensics++ and others, and demonstrates significant improvements in detecting Deepfake, Face2Face, and FaceSwap attacks. The paper also introduces a semi-supervised learning framework to enhance generalization across unseen attack types. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods by up to 4.55% in accuracy, highlighting its effectiveness in handling compressed and low-resolution video content. The study concludes that combining temporal modeling with multi-task learning offers a robust and scalable solution for video-based face manipulation detection.

original_abstract: Neural Networks trained with gradient descent are known to be susceptible to catastrophic forgetting caused by parameter shift during the training process. In the context of Neural Machine Translation (NMT) this results in poor performance on heterogeneous datasets and on sub-tasks like rare phrase translation. On the other hand, non-parametric approaches are immune to forgetting, perfectly complementing the generalization ability of NMT. However, attempts to combine non-parametric or retrieval based approaches with NMT have only been successful on narrow domains, possibly due to over-reliance on sentence level retrieval. We propose a novel n-gram level retrieval approach that relies on local phrase level similarities, allowing us to retrieve neighbors that are useful for translation even when overall sentence similarity is low. We complement this with an expressive neural network, allowing our model to extract information from the noisy retrieved context. We evaluate our semi-parametric NMT approach on a heterogeneous dataset composed of WMT, IWSLT, JRC-Acquis and OpenSubtitles, and demonstrate gains on all 4 evaluation sets. The semi-parametric nature of our approach opens the door for non-parametric domain adaptation, demonstrating strong inference-time adaptation performance on new domains without the need for any parameter updates.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of improving the adequacy of neural machine translation (NMT) systems, which often struggle with accurately translating rare or domain-specific content. Building on prior work that combines NMT with statistical machine translation (SMT) techniques, such as hybrid search and system combination, the paper proposes a novel method that integrates retrieved translation pieces into the NMT decoding process. Unlike previous approaches that rely on fixed-length vectors or rigid phrase-based models, this method dynamically retrieves relevant sentence pairs using a search engine and incorporates their aligned n-grams as "translation pieces" during decoding. These pieces are weighted based on similarity scores and used to guide the NMT model toward more accurate outputs. The proposed approach is evaluated on narrow domain translation tasks, where it achieves significant improvements in BLEU scores while maintaining low computational overhead. The results demonstrate that leveraging external knowledge through retrieval can effectively enhance NMT performance, particularly in scenarios with repetitive or specialized content. The paper concludes that this retrieval-augmented decoding strategy offers a promising direction for improving translation quality without sacrificing fluency or efficiency.

original_abstract: In line with recent advances in neural drug design and sensitivity prediction, we propose a novel architecture for interpretable prediction of anticancer compound sensitivity using a multimodal attention-based convolutional encoder. Our model is based on the three key pillars of drug sensitivity: compounds’ structure in the form of a SMILES sequence, gene expression profiles of tumors and prior knowledge on intracellular interactions from protein-protein interaction networks. We demonstrate that our multiscale convolutional attention-based encoder significantly outperforms a baseline model trained on Morgan fingerprints, a selection of encoders based on SMILES as well as previously reported state of the art for multimodal drug sensitivity prediction (R2 = 0.86 and RMSE = 0.89). Moreover, the explainability of our approach is demonstrated by a thorough analysis of the attention weights. generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately predicting cancer drug sensitivity by integrating multi-omics data with advanced machine learning techniques. Building on prior work that has explored attention-based neural networks, link prediction, and multitask learning, this study proposes a novel dual-layer integrated model that combines cell line similarity networks (CSN) and drug similarity networks (DSN) to enhance prediction accuracy. The method leverages both genomic and chemical features of cancer cell lines and drugs, respectively, and employs a weighted integration strategy to predict drug responses. Unlike previous approaches that rely on single-layer models or traditional regression methods, this paper introduces a more comprehensive framework that captures complex interactions between drugs and cell lines. The proposed model is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating a significant improvement in prediction performance, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.6 for most drugs. The study concludes that the dual-layer network model provides a robust and interpretable approach for predicting drug responses, offering valuable insights for personalized cancer therapy and drug repurposing. This paper represents an application of advanced machine learning in the domain of precision oncology.

original_abstract: The inability to generalize beyond the distribution of a training set is at the core of practical limits of machine learning. We show that the common practice of mixing and shuffling training examples when training deep neural networks is not optimal. On the opposite, partitioning the training data into non-i.i.d. subsets can serve to guide the model to rely on reliable statistical patterns while ignoring spurious correlations in the training data. We demonstrate multiple use cases where these subsets are built using unsupervised clustering, prior knowledge, or other meta-data from existing datasets. The approach is supported by recent results on a causal view of generalization, it is simple to apply, and it demonstrably improves generalization. Applied to the task of visual question answering, we obtain state-of-the-art performance on VQA-CP. We also show improvements over data augmentation using equivalent questions on GQA. Finally, we show a small improvement when training a model simultaneously on VQA v2 and Visual Genome, treating them as two distinct environments rather than one aggregated training set.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the critical issue of language priors in Visual Question Answering (VQA) models, where models often rely on superficial correlations between questions and answers rather than on visual content. Building on prior work that highlights this problem and proposes methods to mitigate it, such as adversarial regularization, dataset balancing, and architectural modifications, this study introduces a novel framework that combines multiple strategies to enhance image grounding while reducing reliance on language biases. The proposed method integrates a bias-aware training procedure with a modified model architecture that explicitly disentangles visual and linguistic processing. The framework is evaluated on both standard and bias-sensitive VQA datasets, including VQA-CP v1 and v2, demonstrating significant improvements in robustness and generalization compared to existing approaches. The results confirm that the proposed method not only reduces the impact of language priors but also enhances model interpretability and performance across varying distributions of answer priors. The paper contributes a new method for improving VQA systems by addressing the limitations of current models in real-world scenarios.

original_abstract: Biological evolution has distilled the experiences of many learners into the general learning algorithms of humans. Our novel meta reinforcement learning algorithm MetaGenRL is inspired by this process. MetaGenRL distills the experiences of many complex agents to meta-learn a low-complexity neural objective function that affects how future individuals will learn. Unlike recent meta-RL algorithms, MetaGenRL can generalize to new environments that are entirely different from those used for meta-training. In some cases, it even outperforms human-engineered RL algorithms. MetaGenRL uses off-policy second-order gradients during meta-training that greatly increase its sample efficiency.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of designing efficient reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms that can adapt quickly to new tasks with minimal training data. Building on recent advances in meta-learning and learning-to-learn frameworks, the paper proposes a novel method that combines the strengths of evolved policy gradients and meta-gradient techniques to automatically discover task-agnostic RL algorithms. Unlike prior work that focuses on learning fixed algorithmic components or optimizing predefined policies, this approach evolves a differentiable loss function that dynamically adapts to the structure of the environment. The proposed method, which integrates meta-learning with gradient-based optimization, enables agents to learn from sparse rewards and generalize across diverse domains. Experimental evaluations on a range of benchmark tasks demonstrate that the method outperforms existing meta-RL and hand-designed algorithms in terms of sample efficiency and task adaptability. The paper concludes that automatically learning algorithmic components through meta-learning represents a promising direction for developing more flexible and robust RL systems.

original_abstract: Reed-Muller (RM) codes are among the oldest, simplest and perhaps most ubiquitous family of codes. They are used in many areas of coding theory in both electrical engineering and computer science. Yet, many of their important properties are still under investigation. This paper covers some of the recent developments regarding the weight enumerator and the capacity-achieving properties of RM codes, as well as some of the algorithmic developments. In particular, the paper discusses the recent connections established between RM codes, thresholds of Boolean functions, polarization theory, hypercontractivity, and the techniques of approximating low weight codewords using lower degree polynomials. It then overviews some of the algorithms with performance guarantees, as well as some of the algorithms with state-of-the-art performances in practical regimes. Finally, the paper concludes with a few open problems.
generated_abstract: This paper investigates the capacity-achieving properties of Reed-Muller (RM) codes on symmetric binary-input memoryless channels, building on recent advances in polarization theory and decoding techniques for RM codes. While polar codes have been rigorously shown to achieve capacity through the polarization phenomenon, RM codes have remained less understood in this context. The paper explores whether RM codes can also achieve capacity by leveraging their inherent structure and the same polarization framework. It demonstrates that, by ordering the rows of the RM generator matrix from lightest to heaviest weight, the conditional mutual information polarizes, similar to polar codes, but potentially more efficiently. This leads to the identification of a "twin-RM code" within the same generator matrix that is provably capacity-achieving on any binary memoryless symmetric channel. The paper further connects this result to prior work on RM code decoding and capacity-achieving properties, showing that RM codes can achieve capacity under appropriate conditions. The study contributes to the theoretical understanding of RM codes and their potential as practical capacity-achieving codes, offering a new perspective on their relationship with polar codes.

original_abstract: To ensure pedestrian friendly streets in the era of automated vehicles, reassessment of current policies, practices, design, rules and regulations of urban areas is of importance. This study investigates pedestrian crossing behaviour, as an important element of urban dynamics that is expected to be affected by the presence of automated vehicles. For this purpose, an interpretable machine learning framework is proposed to explore factors affecting pedestrians' wait time before crossing mid-block crosswalks in the presence of automated vehicles. To collect rich behavioural data, we developed a dynamic and immersive virtual reality experiment, with 180 participants from a heterogeneous population in 4 different locations in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA). Pedestrian wait time behaviour is then analyzed using a data-driven Cox Proportional Hazards (CPH) model, in which the linear combination of the covariates is replaced by a flexible non-linear deep neural network. The proposed model achieved a 5% improvement in goodness of fit, but more importantly, enabled us to incorporate a richer set of covariates. A game theoretic based interpretability method is used to understand the contribution of different covariates to the time pedestrians wait before crossing. Results show that the presence of automated vehicles on roads, wider lane widths, high density on roads, limited sight distance, and lack of walking habits are the main contributing factors to longer wait times. Our study suggested that, to move towards pedestrian-friendly urban areas, national level educational programs for children, enhanced safety measures for seniors, promotion of active modes of transportation, and revised traffic rules and regulations should be considered.
generated_abstract: This paper investigates the impact of external human-machine interfaces (eHMIs) on pedestrian crossing decisions in the context of autonomous vehicles (AVs). Building on prior work that explores pedestrian behavior at crosswalks and the role of communication cues between road users, this study extends the analysis by examining how different eHMI designs influence pedestrian perceptions of safety and crossing intentions. Using a virtual reality environment, the research evaluates five eHMI types and their timing in relation to vehicle behavior, revealing that textual eHMIs are most effective in conveying intent without requiring prior learning. The findings suggest that eHMIs can enhance the efficiency and safety of pedestrian-AV interactions, but their effectiveness depends on design and contextual factors. The paper contributes a novel empirical evaluation of eHMI impact, offering insights for the development of AV communication systems that prioritize clarity and user trust. It concludes that while eHMIs hold promise, further research is needed to optimize their design for diverse urban environments and road user demographics.

original_abstract: Training neural networks is traditionally done by providing a sequence of random mini-batches sampled uniformly from the entire training data. In this work, we analyze the effect of curriculum learning, which involves the non-uniform sampling of mini-batches, on the training of deep networks, and specifically CNNs trained for image recognition. To employ curriculum learning, the training algorithm must resolve 2 problems: (i) sort the training examples by difficulty; (ii) compute a series of mini-batches that exhibit an increasing level of difficulty. We address challenge (i) using two methods: transfer learning from some competitive ``teacher" network, and bootstrapping. In our empirical evaluation, both methods show similar benefits in terms of increased learning speed and improved final performance on test data. We address challenge (ii) by investigating different pacing functions to guide the sampling. The empirical investigation includes a variety of network architectures, using images from CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and subsets of ImageNet. We conclude with a novel theoretical analysis of curriculum learning, where we show how it effectively modifies the optimization landscape. We then define the concept of an ideal curriculum, and show that under mild conditions it does not change the corresponding global minimum of the optimization function.
generated_abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of curriculum learning strategies in training deep neural networks, building on prior work that highlights the importance of structured learning paths for improving model performance. While previous studies have explored curriculum learning through manual design, automated selection, or reverse task generation, this work introduces a novel framework that dynamically adapts the curriculum based on real-time feedback from the learning process. The proposed method integrates principles from transfer learning and reinforcement learning, enabling the system to autonomously adjust the difficulty of training samples in response to the learner's progress. The approach is evaluated on a range of tasks, including sequence-to-sequence learning, image classification, and reinforcement learning environments, demonstrating significant improvements in convergence speed and generalization performance. The results suggest that the proposed curriculum learning framework outperforms existing methods in terms of efficiency and robustness, particularly in scenarios with noisy data or complex task structures. The paper concludes that adaptive curriculum learning represents a promising direction for improving the training of deep neural networks across diverse domains.

original_abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks fostered a newfound interest in generative models, resulting in a swelling wave of new works that new-coming researchers may find formidable to surf. In this paper, we intend to help those researchers, by splitting that incoming wave into six "fronts": Architectural Contributions, Conditional Techniques, Normalization and Constraint Contributions, Loss Functions, Image-to-image Translations, and Validation Metrics. The division in fronts organizes literature into approachable blocks, ultimately communicating to the reader how the area is evolving. Previous surveys in the area, which this works also tabulates, focus on a few of those fronts, leaving a gap that we propose to fill with a more integrated, comprehensive overview. Here, instead of an exhaustive survey, we opt for a straightforward review: our target is to be an entry point to this vast literature, and also to be able to update experienced researchers to the newest techniques.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of generating high-resolution, diverse, and semantically manipulable images using generative adversarial networks (GANs). Building on recent advances in GAN training methodologies, such as progressive growing and style-based architectures, the paper proposes a novel conditional GAN framework that integrates multi-scale adversarial losses with object instance segmentation to enable fine-grained, interactive image editing. Unlike prior work that often struggles with resolution and diversity, the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results in high-resolution image synthesis, producing 2048×1024 photo-realistic images. It also introduces a mechanism for generating diverse outputs from the same input, enhancing user interactivity. The paper evaluates its contributions using both automated metrics and human studies, demonstrating significant improvements in image quality, resolution, and controllability. The work contributes to the field by advancing the practical applicability of GANs in tasks requiring both high fidelity and semantic flexibility.

original_abstract: Local differential privacy (LDP) can provide each user with strong privacy guarantees under untrusted data curators while ensuring accurate statistics derived from privatized data. Due to its powerfulness, LDP has been widely adopted to protect privacy in various tasks (e.g., heavy hitters discovery, probability estimation) and systems (e.g., Google Chrome, Apple iOS). Although ${\epsilon}$-LDP has been proposed for many years, the more general notion of $({\epsilon}, {\delta})$-LDP has only been studied in very few papers, which mainly consider mean estimation for numeric data. Besides, prior solutions achieve $({\epsilon}, {\delta})$-LDP by leveraging Gaussian mechanism, which leads to low accuracy of the aggregated results. In this paper, we propose novel mechanisms that achieve $({\epsilon}, {\delta})$-LDP with high utility in data analytics and machine learning. Specifically, we first design $({\epsilon}, {\delta})$-LDP algorithms for collecting multi-dimensional numeric data, which can ensure higher accuracy than the optimal Gaussian mechanism while guaranteeing strong privacy for each user. Then, we investigate different local protocols for categorical attributes under $({\epsilon}, {\delta})$-LDP. Furthermore, we conduct theoretical analysis on the error bound and variance of the proposed algorithms. Experimental results on real and synthetic datasets demonstrate the high data utility of our proposed algorithms on both simple data statistics and complex machine learning models.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently collecting and analyzing multidimensional data under local differential privacy (LDP), a privacy model where users perturb their data locally before sharing it with an aggregator. While existing LDP solutions either suffer from limited functionality or focus on theoretical aspects, this work proposes a novel system that supports both basic statistics and complex machine learning tasks on data containing numerical and categorical attributes. Building on recent advances in LDP mechanisms, the paper introduces a new framework that improves upon existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, particularly for high-dimensional data. The proposed approach is evaluated through extensive experiments on real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving accurate statistical estimation and machine learning performance under LDP constraints. The paper concludes that the proposed system provides a practical and scalable solution for privacy-preserving data analysis, with significant improvements over prior work in terms of noise variance and usability. This paper presents a new method.

original_abstract: We investigate the combination of actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithms with uniform large-scale experience replay and propose solutions for two challenges: (a) efficient actor-critic learning with experience replay (b) stability of very off-policy learning. We employ those insights to accelerate hyper-parameter sweeps in which all participating agents run concurrently and share their experience via a common replay module. To this end we analyze the bias-variance tradeoffs in V-trace, a form of importance sampling for actor-critic methods. Based on our analysis, we then argue for mixing experience sampled from replay with on-policy experience, and propose a new trust region scheme that scales effectively to data distributions where V-trace becomes unstable. We provide extensive empirical validation of the proposed solution. We further show the benefits of this setup by demonstrating state-of-the-art data efficiency on Atari among agents trained up until 200M environment frames.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of improving sample efficiency and training stability in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) by integrating multiple algorithmic innovations into a unified framework. Building on prior work that introduced distributed architectures, prioritized experience replay, and off-policy learning methods, the paper proposes a novel agent that combines distributional reinforcement learning with advanced policy evaluation techniques. The proposed method incorporates a new policy evaluation algorithm called Distributional Retrace, which extends multi-step off-policy updates to the distributional setting, and introduces a $\beta$-leave-one-out policy gradient algorithm to balance variance and bias. Additionally, the paper presents a prioritized replay algorithm for sequences that leverages temporal locality for more efficient learning. The agent is evaluated on the Atari 2600 benchmark, where it achieves state-of-the-art performance with significantly improved sample efficiency and faster training times compared to existing methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively combines multiple DRL advancements, leading to more robust and efficient learning across a wide range of tasks.

original_abstract: The design of deep graph models still remains to be investigated and the crucial part is how to explore and exploit the knowledge from different hops of neighbors in an efficient way. In this paper, we propose a novel RNN-like deep graph neural network architecture by incorporating AdaBoost into the computation of network; and the proposed graph convolutional network called AdaGCN~(AdaBoosting Graph Convolutional Network) has the ability to efficiently extract knowledge from high-order neighbors and integrate knowledge from different hops of neighbors into the network in an AdaBoost way. We also present the architectural difference between AdaGCN and existing graph convolutional methods to show the benefits of our proposal. Finally, extensive experiments demonstrate the state-of-the-art prediction performance and the computational advantage of our approach AdaGCN.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of designing efficient and expressive graph neural networks (GNNs) for semi-supervised learning tasks, building on prior work that generalizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to graph-structured data. While existing methods such as Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), Graph Attention Networks (GATs), and MixHop have made significant progress, they often suffer from limitations in capturing multi-scale neighborhood relationships, over-smoothing with depth, and computational inefficiency. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes a novel architecture that integrates multi-scale neighborhood aggregation with adaptive information propagation, inspired by the principles of spectral graph theory and the insights from simplified GCN models. The proposed method enables deeper networks without over-smoothing by decoupling representation transformation and propagation, and it incorporates sparsity regularization to enhance interpretability and scalability. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the new architecture outperforms state-of-the-art methods in node classification tasks while maintaining linear computational complexity. The paper concludes that the proposed approach provides a more flexible and powerful framework for learning graph representations, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data and complex graph structures.

original_abstract: This paper seeks to answer a simple but fundamental question: what role can non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) play in massive multi-in multi-out (MIMO)? It is well established that power-domain NOMA schemes can outperform conventional orthogonal multiple access schemes in cellular networks. However, this fact does not imply that NOMA is the most efficient way to communicate in massive MIMO setups, where the base stations have many more antennas than there are users in the cell. These setups are becoming the norm in future networks and are usually studied by assuming spatial multiplexing of the users using linear multi-user beamforming. To answer the above-mentioned question, we analyze and compare the performance achieved by NOMA and multi-user beamforming in both non-line-of-sight and line-of-sight scenarios. We reveal that the latter scheme gives the highest average sum rate in massive MIMO setups. We also identify specific cases where NOMA is the better choice in massive MIMO and explain how NOMA plays an essential role in creating a hybrid of NOMA and multi-user beamforming that is shown to perform better than two standalone schemes do.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of integrating non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) with massive MIMO systems in scenarios where channel state information (CSI) is limited or acquired through training pilots. Building on prior work that explores the potential of massive MIMO and NOMA separately, the paper identifies a gap in the literature regarding the performance of NOMA in massive MIMO systems under practical training-based CSI acquisition. It proposes a novel NOMA scheme that leverages the benefits of massive MIMO while minimizing the feedback overhead through shared pilot signaling. The paper evaluates the achievable rates of the proposed scheme under different pilot configurations and compares it with traditional orthogonal multiple access (OMA) approaches. The results show that the proposed NOMA scheme achieves significant performance gains over OMA when downlink CSI is available, but its effectiveness diminishes with increasing user groups, suggesting a trade-off between NOMA and multi-user beamforming. The study concludes that the proposed method offers a viable solution for enhancing spectral efficiency in massive MIMO systems with limited feedback, provided the number of users is moderate. The paper is an empirical study that contributes to the understanding of NOMA in the context of massive MIMO with practical CSI constraints.

original_abstract: In [1, 2], we have explored the theoretical aspects of feature extraction optimization processes for solving largescale problems and overcoming machine learning limitations. Majority of optimization algorithms that have been introduced in [1, 2] guarantee the optimal performance of supervised learning, given offline and discrete data, to deal with curse of dimensionality (CoD) problem. These algorithms, however, are not tailored for solving emerging learning problems. One of the important issues caused by online data is lack of sufficient samples per class. Further, traditional machine learning algorithms cannot achieve accurate training based on limited distributed data, as data has proliferated and dispersed significantly. Machine learning employs a strict model or embedded engine to train and predict which still fails to learn unseen classes and sufficiently use online data. In this chapter, we introduce these challenges elaborately. We further investigate Meta-Learning (MTL) algorithm, and their application and promises to solve the emerging problems by answering how autonomous agents can learn to learn?.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of few-shot learning by proposing a novel method that integrates hallucination with meta-learning to enhance performance when only a small number of examples are available. Building on existing approaches such as Matching Networks, Relation Networks, and Prototypical Networks, the paper departs by introducing a "hallucinator" that generates synthetic examples to augment the limited training data. This is combined with a meta-learner to optimize both components jointly, enabling the model to better generalize from few examples. The proposed method is evaluated on standard few-shot benchmarks, including ImageNet and Omniglot, and demonstrates significant improvements in classification accuracy, particularly in low-shot scenarios. The paper concludes that incorporating hallucination into meta-learning provides a powerful and flexible framework for few-shot learning, offering state-of-the-art results and suggesting promising directions for future research. The paper is a new method contribution.

original_abstract: Edge computing is an emerging concept based on distributing computing, storage, and control services closer to end network nodes. Edge computing lies at the heart of the fifth generation (5G) wireless systems and beyond. While current state-of-the-art networks communicate, compute, and process data in a centralized manner (at the cloud), for latency and compute-centric applications, both radio access and computational resources must be brought closer to the edge, harnessing the availability of computing and storage-enabled small cell base stations in proximity to the end devices. Furthermore, the network infrastructure must enable a distributed edge decision-making service that learns to adapt to the network dynamics with minimal latency and optimize network deployment and operation accordingly. This article will provide a fresh look to the concept of edge computing by first discussing the applications that the network edge must provide, with a special emphasis on the ensuing challenges in enabling ultra-reliable and low-latency edge computing services for mission-critical applications such as virtual reality (VR), vehicle-to-everything (V2X), edge artificial intelligence (AI), and so forth. Furthermore, several case studies where the edge is key are explored followed by insights and prospect for future work.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of achieving ultra-reliable and low-latency communication (URLLC) in 5G and beyond networks by proposing a novel framework that integrates mobility management, task offloading, and edge intelligence. Building on prior work in user-centric mobility management, dual connectivity, and edge learning, the paper departs by introducing a unified approach that jointly optimizes handover, resource allocation, and distributed machine learning under stringent reliability and latency constraints. The proposed method leverages stochastic geometry, mean-field games, and Lyapunov optimization to manage dynamic user mobility and channel conditions while ensuring task offloading meets ultra-reliable requirements. A key contribution is the development of a two-timescale mechanism that adapts user-server associations and resource allocations in response to both temporal and spatial network dynamics. The paper concludes that the proposed framework significantly improves system performance in terms of energy efficiency, reliability, and latency, as demonstrated through extensive simulations and comparisons with existing methods. This work represents an application of advanced theoretical models to real-world edge computing and communication scenarios, offering a practical solution for mission-critical 5G and beyond applications.

original_abstract: Automatic Post-Editing (APE) aims to correct systematic errors in a machine translated text. This is primarily useful when the machine translation (MT) system is not accessible for improvement, leaving APE as a viable option to improve translation quality as a downstream task - which is the focus of this thesis. This field has received less attention compared to MT due to several reasons, which include: the limited availability of data to perform a sound research, contrasting views reported by different researchers about the effectiveness of APE, and limited attention from the industry to use APE in current production pipelines. In this thesis, we perform a thorough investigation of APE as a downstream task in order to: i) understand its potential to improve translation quality; ii) advance the core technology - starting from classical methods to recent deep-learning based solutions; iii) cope with limited and sparse data; iv) better leverage multiple input sources; v) mitigate the task-specific problem of over-correction; vi) enhance neural decoding to leverage external knowledge; and vii) establish an online learning framework to handle data diversity in real-time. All the above contributions are discussed across several chapters, and most of them are evaluated in the APE shared task organized each year at the Conference on Machine Translation. Our efforts in improving the technology resulted in the best system at the 2017 APE shared task, and our work on online learning received a distinguished paper award at the Italian Conference on Computational Linguistics. Overall, outcomes and findings of our work have boost interest among researchers and attracted industries to examine this technology to solve real-word problems.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of improving the quality of machine translation (MT) output through automatic post-editing (APE), focusing on the integration of neural machine translation (NMT) models with quality estimation (QE) techniques. The approach leverages log-linear combinations and sequence-level training objectives to ensure consistency with evaluation metrics and reduce exposure bias. original_abstract: We consider a variant of the classic Ski Rental online algorithm with applications to machine learning. In our variant, we allow the skier access to a black-box machine-learning algorithm that provides an estimate of the probability that there will be at most a threshold number of ski-days. We derive a class of optimal randomized algorithms to determine the strategy that minimizes the worst-case expected competitive ratio for the skier given a prediction from the machine learning algorithm,and analyze the performance and robustness of these algorithms.
generated_abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of integrating machine learning predictions into online algorithms to improve their performance while maintaining robustness against prediction errors. It extends the approach by considering the impact of prediction accuracy on algorithm performance and introduces a method that gracefully degrades when predictions are unreliable. The paper applies this framework to the ski-rental problem, showing how average-case analyses can guide decision-making and yield better practical outcomes than traditional worst-case guarantees. The proposed approach is evaluated both theoretically and empirically, demonstrating that it achieves improved competitive ratios when predictions are accurate, while maintaining worst-case performance bounds.
